headline: AI chip stocks fell sharply again on Tuesday, with South Korea's main index down more than 6%, in what Reuters calls the strongest sign yet that the AI trade is turning.
score_reason: Pool 8 kept: the Reuters analysis was read in full and its market figures match the headline; it reads the mood of the market and is not a forecast.
importance_line: Five days of selling in South Korea and a likely sixth straight fall in the main US chip index matter first to savers and pension holders in chip-heavy funds, then to lenders financing the AI build-out, then to chip makers such as Kioxia and Micron; the doubt is that the investor Reuters quotes blames positioning and borrowing costs, not weaker AI demand.
summary: Reuters reports in an analysis that Tuesday 13 Oct 2026 brought the heaviest selling of AI supplier shares since late July, the strongest sign yet that the mood on the AI trade is shifting amid worries that rising interest rates could derail a spending boom bigger than the historic US railroad boom: South Korean chipmaker shares fell for a fifth straight day, taking the KOSPI, the country's main share index, down more than 6%, Kioxia, a Japanese memory-chip maker, lost 13%, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, the main US gauge of chip shares, was heading for a sixth straight fall. It continues the slide we carried on 12 Oct 2026, when South Korea's index fell 3.65% and Broadcom's chief executive said capital was his company's biggest constraint; new today are the fifth day of Korean selling, the International Monetary Fund's warning that the consequences of an AI correction "could be global", and the view of Marc Velan, head of investments at Lucerne Asset Management in Singapore, that the session says more about positioning and the cost of capital than about weaker AI demand, although "Korea could be an early warning of a broader shakeout".
notes: Reuters page returned HTTP 401; the Reuters wire text was read in The Lufkin Daily News copy. Link kept to the Reuters original. Follow-up of the 12 Oct 2026 chip-share fall and Broadcom items; what is new is the fifth day of Korean selling, the IMF warning and Velan's comment.
